I need authoritative, documented facts (official wikis, official dedicated-server docs, Valve developer docs) — not guesses — about how Steam Workshop content is activated on a DEDICATED SERVER for each of these 6 games. This is for a real production feature: Nxeon (a game-hosting company) writes a Steam Workshop ID into the server's config/launch args, and the dedicated server binary itself is supposed to fetch/mount the content on boot — Nxeon never downloads or mirrors the file itself. I need to know, per game, whether that "pure config write" assumption is actually true, and exactly what config mechanism to use.

For EACH of these 6 games, research and report:
1. The correct Steam AppID for the DEDICATED SERVER (not the client game) — e.g. via SteamDB or the official wiki.
2. The exact, documented mechanism to make a subscribed/chosen Workshop item active on a dedicated server: is it a launch argument (e.g. `-mod=`, `+host_workshop_collection`), a config file line (e.g. an .ini or .cfg key listing Workshop IDs), or does it require running `steamcmd +workshop_download_item <appid> <fileid>` once so the file is cached, THEN referencing it in config? Quote the exact key/arg name as documented.
3. Whether the dedicated server process fetches Workshop content itself on boot (pure config-write, no download step Nxeon needs to do) OR whether an explicit steamcmd `workshop_download_item` step is required first before the ID is usable.
4. A link/citation to the source (official wiki page, Valve dev docs, or the game's official dedicated server guide).
5. If you cannot find authoritative documentation for a game, say so explicitly — do not guess or infer from unrelated games.

Games:
1. ARK: Survival Evolved (the ORIGINAL, ASE — appid used by most hosts is 376030 for server; confirm) — Steam Workshop mods via -mods= launch parameter, confirm exact syntax (comma-separated mod IDs?).
2. Unturned — RocketMod/OpenMod aside, focus specifically on Steam Workshop MAPS/items — the WorkshopDownloadConfig.json mechanism (server config file listing Workshop File IDs) — confirm exact filename and JSON key names, and confirm the dedicated server itself downloads content anonymously via SteamCMD workshop content depot without a download step from us.
3. Don't Starve Together (DST) — the "cluster_id" / mod setup — confirm exact file name (a `dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua` file with `ServerModSetup("id")` calls, typically in the Don't Starve Together dedicated server root, separate from world's modoverrides.lua) and whether the game itself fetches content via steam_appid 343050 on boot.
4. Squad — official Workshop support: confirm launch argument or config file (Squad's `ServerConfig` or a Mods list) and the dedicated server appid (403240 for server?).
5. Empyrion – Galactic Survival — verify: does the DEDICATED SERVER actually support Steam Workshop natively (via `dedicated.yaml` mod scenario/workshop settings) or does it truly require manual file placement as some sources claim? This is disputed — resolve it with an authoritative source (official Empyrion wiki / Eleon forums dedicated server docs).
6. Soulmask — Steam Workshop just launched (per official announcement, per the game's own "Modkits" tooling) — find the dedicated server documentation (if any exists yet) for referencing Workshop mod IDs in the server's config, and its dedicated server appid.

Report in a structured per-game format. Be honest about confidence level per game (confirmed via official docs vs inferred vs unconfirmed). Keep total report under 900 words plus citations.

## Overview

The WorkshopDownloadConfig.json file is used to configure the workshop download settings for your server and allows you to specify which mods and maps should be downloaded from the Steam Workshop and installed on your server.

Locate WorkshopDownloadConfig.json in your server folder (Servers/YourServer/), make sure "Workshop": true is enabled, and add Steam Workshop File IDs under "File_IDs". Restart your server after saving changes.

**ARK: Survival Evolved (ASE)** — Confirmed.
1. Dedicated server AppID: **376030** (SteamDB: "ARK: Survival Evolved Dedicated Server").
2. Two documented mechanisms, both real: (a) launch parameter `-mods=<ModID1>[,<ModID2>...]` (comma-separated, no spaces), and (b) `GameUserSettings.ini` under `[ServerSettings]`, key `ActiveMods=ModID1,ModID2,ModID3` (comma-separated, leftmost = highest priority). A third flag, `-automanagedmods`, auto-downloads/updates mods listed in `Game.ini` under `[ModInstaller]`.
3. Pure config-write is true — the server binary downloads/updates workshop mods itself on boot via its built-in Steam mod-download system; no external `steamcmd workshop_download_item` step is documented as required.
4. Source: ARK Official Community Wiki, Server configuration — https://ark.wiki.gg/wiki/Server_configuration ; AppID via SteamDB — https://steamdb.info/app/376030/info/

**Unturned** — Confirmed.
1. Dedicated-server AppID note: Unturned uses one Steam app for client+server; workshop content ties to appid 304930 (no separate dedicated-server appid exists/needed — worth flagging since your task assumed a distinct dedicated AppID pattern).
2. Config file: **`WorkshopDownloadConfig.json`** (per-server, in `Servers/<ServerName>/`), boolean `"Workshop": true`, array key **`"File_IDs"`** listing numeric Workshop File IDs, e.g. `"File_IDs": [1753134636]`.
3. Pure config-write is true — official docs state: "During server startup, any specified mods (and their dependencies) will be installed and updated." No manual download step needed for public items (private/unlisted items cannot be fetched this way since the server can't authenticate a Steam account).
4. Source: official developer docs (Smartly Dressed Games) — https://docs.smartlydressedgames.com/en/latest/servers/server-hosting.html

**Don't Starve Together (DST)** — Confirmed, high confidence.
1. AppID 343050 (server binary, same ID for Windows/Linux) — SteamDB: https://steamdb.info/app/343050/
2. File: **`dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua`**, located in the dedicated server install's `mods/` folder (i.e. `.../Don't Starve Together Dedicated Server/mods/dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua`) — separate from the per-cluster `modoverrides.lua`. Exact syntax: `ServerModSetup("345692228")` per mod, or `ServerModCollectionSetup("<collectionID>")` for a workshop collection.
3. Pure config-write is true — this file "is run on boot and will download any mods or collection of mods that are setup in the file." Override flags exist: `-skip_update_server_mods` / `-only_update_server_mods`.
4. Source: community-maintained but technically detailed guide (github.com/mathielo/dst-dedicated-server) corroborating the standard Klei-documented mechanism; Klei's own official Don't Starve Wiki guide (dontstarve.wiki.gg / fandom "Guides/Don't Starve Together Dedicated Servers") describes the same file/function names.

**Squad** — Partially confirmed, moderate confidence only.
1. Dedicated server AppID confirmed: **403240** (SteamDB, Steam Support wizard both list this). Workshop items themselves are browsed/downloaded under the **game's** AppID **393380**, not 403240 — important distinction for a `workshop_download_item` call.
2. Mechanism is genuinely unclear from primary sources: the official Squad Wiki page ("Uploading a mod to a dedicated server") was inaccessible in this research (blocked/paywalled fetch, 402/CAPTCHA on every attempt). Multiple independent third-party host docs (GGServers, XGamingServer, Shockbyte, LOW.MS) converge on: a "Workshop Mod IDs" field/list, comma-separated, that the server (or the hosting control panel wrapping it) resolves via SteamCMD `+workshop_download_item 393380 <ModID>`, placing the mod into `SquadGame/Plugins/Mods/`. But several of these describe their own **control-panel UI**, not necessarily the raw server binary's native config key — I could not verify an exact `.cfg` key name or launch-arg name from an official source.
3. **Cannot fully confirm "pure config write."** Evidence is mixed: some sources say the dedicated server (or wrapper like the `cm2network/squad` Docker image's `MODS` env var) downloads content itself on boot; others explicitly describe manually running `steamcmd +workshop_download_item 393380 <ModID>` and copying the resulting folder into `SquadGame/Plugins/Mods/` before the server will recognize it. **Empyrion – Galactic Survival** — Resolved: the "manual placement" claim is correct, not the "native workshop" claim.
1. Dedicated server AppID: **530870** (SteamDB, Steam Support wizard).
2. Config file `dedicated.yaml`, under `GameConfig`, key **`CustomScenario`** — but this key only takes a **local folder name string** under `Content/Scenarios/`. There is no yaml key that takes a raw Steam Workshop File ID or triggers a download.

Multiple independent host docs (Host Havoc, GTXGaming, Pingperfect, 4Netplayers) all describe the same required manual flow: subscribe to the Workshop scenario as a player, locate it under `steamapps/workshop/content/383120/<fileid>/`, copy that folder into the server's `Content/Scenarios/` directory, rename it away from the numeric ID, then reference that folder name in `CustomScenario`. So Nxeon cannot do a pure config write for Empyrion — it must run a steamcmd/anon download step for the workshop item and place the files itself before referencing it.
4. Source: Empyrion Official Wiki — https://empyrion.fandom.com/wiki/Guide/Setting_Up_Dedicated_Server ; AppID https://steamdb.info/app/530870/info/ ; corroborating manual-placement guides: https://hosthavoc.com/wiki/game-servers/empyrion-galactic-survival/add-workshop-scenario , https://www.gtxgaming.co.uk/clientarea/knowledgebase/709/How-to-install-Workshop-scenarios-on-your-Empyrion-server..html

1. Dedicated server AppIDs: **3017310** (Windows), **3017300** (Linux) — both installable anonymously via SteamCMD. Game client AppID (do not install on server) is 2646460. Confirmed via SteamDB: https://steamdb.info/app/3017310/info/

Pure config-write appears true per these sources — "The mods should automatically download and activate when the server starts," i.e., the dedicated binary fetches Workshop content itself on boot referencing the game's Workshop depot (2646460's workshop). No explicit `steamcmd workshop_download_item` step was documented as required.
4. Confidence: **moderate, not fully authoritative** — I could not locate an official Steam-hosted "Soulmask dedicated server documentation" page or an Eleon/official-wiki equivalent; the Soulmask Fandom "Modkits Overview" and "Private Server" pages exist but were not directly fetchable (fandom blocking).
